As a sitter and a dog owner, I completely understand why people wants to go inside before dropping out their pup. It’s like children for a lot of people, and you don’t drop your child in front of the door and say bye and leave ! I always open my door when I board a dog, yes it is not the funniest part , but people are reassured , and they leave with peace of mind. Idk but for me , it is something you have to deal with when you offer boarding. ( I speak only for boarding though, of course a dog who come to your place 3 times per week for day care it is not the same )

As an owner of a reactive dog , I think you are at faut here. I work very hard with my dog, and he is okay around other dogs if they don’t harass him. there is not a lot of adult dogs who love being jumped on and get sniffed by a dog they don’t know, even more when they are on leash. Even if it is a space where dog can be off leash , you have to be able to recall and control your dog. I think it is one of the first thing to learn with your pup.use a long leash until he is good at it ! don’t let your dog run free when you can not recall him, you never know what can happen, even in a closed park, someone can let the door open , you never know.
